context:
Goal: a child repo's CI catches a copied claude-settings rule.
Problem (rule): the child's CI needs the parent's rule text to compare against.
Based on (read): the plan, part c; the ste-lint already checks out claude-settings at a pinned sha (decision action-pins-follow-sessions).
Departs from: main gives child CI no copy check — adds a pinned checkout of claude-settings in child CI.

lastAnswer.note: isnt there a better way than both of these options tho

options.gain: One home for the rule ids; nothing copied into the child.
options.label: Yes: a pinned checkout, as the ste-lint does (recommended)
options.lose: The pin must be bumped to see new rules (the same chore as today's pins).

options.label: No: copy the rule ids into each child
options.lose: The copy goes stale, and it breaks your rule that an allow list points at the constant, never a copy.

reply: You picked a, and asked for a better way. Two are better. 1) Put the copy check inside the shared lint action that every child already pins. Then no new CI step is needed, and the bot that bumps pins keeps it current. This is a done better, and the lane builds it this way. 2) claude-settings scans every child repo at its latest version on a schedule, with no pin at all. It always uses the newest rules, but it finds a copy after it merges, not before. Your a stands, built as 1). Say 'parent scans' if you want 2) instead. Home: step one-home-check.
short: One-home Q3 of 5: child CI reads claude-settings at a pinned version?
title: One-home check, question 3 of 5: should a child repo's CI read claude-settings at a pinned version to find copied rules?
